#2705. Remy Rees-Dottin: Fareham to Belgrade and life as a professional footballer in Serbia

In the latest instalment of GOAL's 'Brits Abroad' series, a man that graced the Premier League with Bournemouth talks hiking in Kyrgyzstan, fanatical flare-wielding supporters and what to do in Serbia

There was a time not all that long ago when British footballers plying their trade abroad were rarer than hen's teeth. Individual reluctance to leave geographical comfort zones led to collective wings being clipped.

This is, however, a brave new world, with cultural advancement meaning that no corner of the planet should be considered too far-flung. Flying the nest and enjoying a different way of life is now an experience to be embraced, rather than feared.

Of course there are challenges - professional and personal hurdles that need to be cleared on the way - but why not embrace those instead of shying away from them? More and more players are adopting that mindset.

Taking that into account, and as we are forever told that travel broadens the mind, GOAL will be helping to tell the story of some of the intrepid explorers that have broken down barriers and found themselves in a position to impart both sporting and holidaying wisdom.

Next up is Remy Rees-Dottin, a man who has traded the south coast of England for the Serbian capital of Belgrade…

Rees-Dottin graduated out of the academy system at Bournemouth

"I started playing grassroots from a very young age, like four or five, for my local team Gosport Borough. Then I was picked up quite early. I was at Chelsea from six until nine and then I was going back and forth between Southampton and Chelsea up until signing my first contract - which I signed at Southampton just because it was a bit closer to where I lived and the driving for my parents was a lot. I was at Southampton until 12, when I was released, and then at Bournemouth until this summer.

"It was definitely hard getting released because at that young of an age, it really takes a toll on you mentally. I can see from my parents' perspective that they were quite worried about me because it's a time where a lot of kids would stop playing football and maybe go back to grassroots. I did a trial at Fulham as soon as I got released, but the driving was crazy - it was about an hour-and-a-half each way and with school and everything it's just a lot. So I did a trial at Bournemouth, went to an open trial, got accepted for a six-week trial, which I did three weeks of and then joined there.

"The facilities were very different. We were category three at the time at Bournemouth, so going from a category one academy to category three was a bit like 'what am I getting myself into?' But I really enjoyed it there, especially at the start. It brought back my love for the game and I was having fun. I had great team-mates, great coaches, so I think it really brought me to where I am now."

Premier League bow was made against Newcastle in January 2025

"I was completely thrown in at the deep end with my debut! We broke up for the Christmas break with the 21s around December 22 and me and my girlfriend went to the north of Wales - we had a cabin that we stayed in for a little festive break. Came back in for 21s training on December 27 and my coach came up to me and was like 'just to warn you, you may be needed for first team training tomorrow before they travel to Fulham so bring a bag just in case they need the extra player'.

"It was only my second ever first team session. Went in with my bag not expecting anything and then got to the group chat and was told that I was travelling. From then on, I was with them for the next three weeks and made my FA Cup debut at home - wasn't really expecting that! The week after we travelled to St James' Park and I came on for the last minute of that game, which was definitely the best moment of my life let alone career!"

The plan was always to leave English football at some point

"For me, I think my dreams growing up were a little bit different. I've never really been set on 'I want to be a Premier League player, I want to play for the best teams in England'. I was always looking to play abroad. The big thing for me, my meaning of life, I want to explore as much as I can. I want to see God's creation on this earth. I want to see as much as I can in my lifetime.

"So going abroad to play football is such a blessing, such an opportunity that I think I had to take. In the summer I didn't know if I'd be leaving permanently or on loan, I just knew that I wanted to play some men's football. The season before, I was looking to go on loan abroad but I had an injury at the end of the window. I spoke to my agent and said 'if it's a possibility, I would love to go abroad, whether it's on loan or permanently'.

"I didn't really care where it would be, I just wanted a bit of a change and a bit of a different experience to playing in the English pyramid. Luckily, Cukaricki came in for me quite early in the window and we waited out to see the other options. I came in permanently and I'm over the moon."

Several options were considered before settling on Cukaricki

"I wanted to stay in Europe for the time being because I'm only 20, it's still my first proper move away. Fareham up to Bournemouth, away from my parents at 16, was a bit of a change but moving to a completely different country is something else. They came in for me quite early in the window. I had a couple other clubs - some League Two clubs, a couple of League One clubs. I was waiting on a team in Switzerland and a team in Croatia as well, so I was delaying this one just because I wanted to make the best decision.

"This is such a big step, moving into men's football, so I waited this one out and luckily they waited around for me. They were very happy to wait and I was able to get the move done. It's hard because obviously there's part of me that would have loved to stay in the English pyramid and been close to my parents, close to my girlfriend, but I do quite like trying new things and experiencing things that other players might be a bit too anxious or afraid to do. I like to take that step.

"One of my favorite hobbies is hiking - I like going to random countries across the world and exploring things that maybe some people are a bit too afraid to or don't maybe want to do, especially alone. I think that played a part in doing this move and making me comfortable to do this."

Settling into a new home has been relatively straightforward

"I've really enjoyed it so far. It is a lot better of a city than I expected. I did my research but prior to Cukaricki making an offer, I knew nothing about the country. The language is difficult, obviously they don't use the English alphabet so learning that is quite tricky! I've only got down maybe three words at the moment but I'm trying.

"A lot of people do speak good English, my team-mates speak good English, and if you go into the shops there's always someone to help. The people here are very friendly, they're always offering to help me as a foreigner, which is good. Food is really good. I haven't had any worries with that, I'm able to get everything I need. I'm really well supported by the club as well - getting an apartment for me to live in was all sorted by them. Directing me to what shops to buy from to get certain foods, that's all sorted by them.

"I haven't had anything come up where I'm majorly struggling. I don't have to panic at all for anything. I've been able to go home to see my parents on international breaks and when we've had a couple days off, which is also nice because the flight isn't too far. I've really enjoyed it and I'm glad I took this step out of my comfort zone to come here."

Obvious linguistical challenges have been faced in the Serbian capital

"I really am trying my hardest because last year when I picked up my injury, because I had so much time on my hands, I got a German tutor. I was able to pick that up quite well. I was on and off doing that and then when I found out I was coming here, I tried to start getting some simple phrases into my vocabulary to help me out. I try as much as I can. I'm looking things up, I'm doing my research to try and get a better understanding of not only the language but the culture as well, as certain customs are obviously different to England.

"I'm working hard trying to do it. It's definitely difficult though, I've only got a few words and phrases but as time goes on, I know I'll be able to adapt to it a bit better and I'll be able to speak a bit better to team-mates and staff and people I go past in the streets."

Rees-Dottin looks to make the most of free time away from football

"I think the biggest cultural difference for me, which I don't think it's weird but just not what I expected, is that their work-life balance is really good here. Even for me coming from 21s football, I'll be in from maybe 9am and I'll leave the training ground at half three/four. Here, I'll be maybe in at nine and I'll be back in my apartment by midday.

"I may go shopping or just have a little stroll around and you see so many people compared to England. Everyone back home would be working, but you see so many people just relaxing either at home on their balconies or having a slow day at a cafe with their friends or family, which is really nice to see. It's a lot more relaxed, a lot calmer here than I expected and obviously from what I've lived for 20 years in England."

Belgrade fortress has been declared a Monument of Culture of Exceptional Importance

"Belgrade is really nice. It's definitely not what I expected. There's a really nice juxtaposition of old Yugoslavian-style apartments and concrete buildings mixed in as well - the newer, modern buildings, full glass skyscrapers and apartment complexes. I've had quite a few walks out and about. My girlfriend came for a couple weeks as well, we had some nice walks - found a fortress up at the top of the city centre. There are some really nice cafes and sunset/sunrise spots.

"I'm trying to experience as much as I can while I'm here because obviously I don't know how long I'll be here. I want to take in as much as I can and see as much as I can. I'm trying to do it as one of the locals would do it, I'm not trying to be here as a tourist because I live here now, I'm not here visiting. I want to experience what they experience so I'm trying to go to more local cafes and experience the local lifestyle and what the people that have lived here their whole lives have experienced."

Costs are generally low but fresh meat can come at a premium

"I'd say the cost of living is definitely cheaper here, especially food wise - some of that is crazy cheap. The apartment I'm in is a lot cheaper than something you find in the UK. If you're coming for a long weekend, you'll definitely realise how cheap it is here. Me and my team-mate went out a couple of days ago for coffee, some toast and a pastry and in London what we got would probably cost 25 quid each. I think it cost us 23 for the both of us.

"In terms of what's more expensive, I'd say meat products can sometimes be a bit pricey. One thing that I find hard is when you go to the supermarket back home, you go to Aldi or Asda or something, you can just go down the aisle and pick up what you want. Here, a lot of their meat is behind a deli counter and sometimes they don't always speak the best English so it's hard to get what you want. There's an organic supermarket that I order from and I get steak from there, which can cost about maybe 22 pounds - which is more expensive than some shops in the UK, but I'm getting a cut which is the biggest steak I've ever seen so you get what you pay for.

"Stuff that isn't local here is definitely a bit more expensive to get. There's some stuff that you can't get, or I haven't seen yet. I'm missing tea! I haven't found proper tea bags here yet, which is kind of annoying. I forgot to bring some back from the last visit home. Some stuff you may miss, but you can always get it when you go home. Ordering stuff here is a bit tricky, you can't just order anything you want off Amazon. I mean there's always ways around it - shopping here is really easy, they have all kinds of shops that you'll see in the UK, so that's not an issue."

There is no excuse not to get out and about in Belgrade

"If I'm in season, after a training day or a match day, I'll come back and maybe call my girlfriend, my family. I do like to get out and about. I'm a big nature person. There's a few parks around where I live, which I like to go for a walk in, and then there's a nice mountainous region further in the south which I'm yet to visit but that's something I definitely want to do because obviously that's one of my main hobbies.

"In the off-season, I'll almost always try to book something to go hiking. I went to Central Asia this summer and spent four days there hiking. If I can't get out, say the weather's really bad, I'll stick on some hiking videos or some camping videos and just relax my body and get ready for the next day."

The spectacular Swiss Alps delivered one memorable vacation

"It was really random how the hiking started. I was a scholar at Bournemouth, I was living in digs with my host family, and I would come back from training and I'd just be in bed and watching YouTube. I'd have the auto videos on and a hiking video would always come on. I suddenly just got really interested in it.

"I randomly spoke to my team-mates about it and I booked a holiday with one of my ex-team-mates to Switzerland - to Lauterbrunnen in the Swiss Alps. It was some of the best three days I've ever had! Since then, the year after, as soon as pre-season started, I was looking forward to the off-season to get away again. Me and my girlfriend went to Chamonix to do the French Alps - I went hiking there for a few days and just relaxed. This summer was the big one as I went to Kyrgyzstan - solo as well, which was quite tricky. It was crazy. It's two five-hour flights and then a seven-hour taxi! But it was really nice. That was my first time camping as well, because the last ones I would stay in a cabin or a hotel but this one I wanted to take another step out of my comfort zone. I spent three days there, two nights, and it just takes that edge off.

"You're so stressed and you're so in the zone all season for nine/10 months, so as much as people say you've exercised for nine months, you've been playing football, why are you going walking for another week? It's just my way to relax. It's my way to be by myself. I'm a bit more introverted, so it's nice to be in my own space and just explore and see what else is on this earth, rather than maybe sitting in and relaxing. This is my way of being able to relax and calm my mind."

Rees-Dottin's interest in hiking has taken him as far as Central Asia

"I would probably say the Kyrgyzstan trip was the most scenic, just because some of the mountain ranges are incredible. One that I did, I reached just shy of a 4000-metre peak, which was crazy. I've never been that high before and you feel it with the air - the air's getting a bit thinner, it's a bit hard to breathe, but the challenge is nice as well. You're walking all this time, maybe for three hours through dense forest, and then you open up to this amazing view and it's what you've worked for in the last three hours.

"It's nice that I'm able to challenge myself while still finding it relaxing. My brain's still ticking, rather than if I was sat at home on the sofa. I'm able to get out and about but it's still my way of relaxing."

Reaching the summit of Mount Everest remains a long-term future goal

"I've certainly got a bucket list. There's a couple places I want to tick off. I had a little thought that after I retire I want to get into mountaineering, and I suggested Everest. My mum wasn't really having it so we'll see closer to the time! The bucket list is definitely filling up. Scrolling through social media, I see a place and I'm like 'that looks amazing' and I'll do a little research and put it on the bucket list.

"It's getting full but you only have maybe five or six weeks in the off season where you're able to get things done. Obviously you want to spend time with your family and I want to spend time with my girlfriend and do other bits, so it's definitely hard to get through but it is looking good. I'm excited when that off season comes around as I know I have something that I'm looking forward to doing."

Passionate supporters in Serbia know how to put on a show

"I would say the first thing is to find a local cafe. There's a lot of touristy cafes, which are always really nice and they do use local ingredients, but the local cafes are really friendly, really welcoming, they'll speak good English. Everyone in the country speaks good English, so that's a good thing. The coffee's really nice here. They have really nice pastries, so it's definitely something to try out.

"I would suggest going to the Belgrade fortress, that's probably my favourite place that I've been to - it's near the city centre, which is nice as if you're doing a short visit you may want to stay in the city where it's close to everything. It's really old infrastructure and looks out on the Belgrade waterfront. You can get really nice sunsets there if the sky's clear.

"A third thing, I would suggest going to watch a football game. Even if you're not a football fan, I think the atmosphere is just incredible here. The fans really love their clubs! I remember the first day I came, [Red Star] Belgrade were playing Partizan and I put it on the TV and I'd never seen anything like it - the flares going off, fireworks. When we played Partizan a few weeks ago, we're a smaller club but they set off loads of red flares and black flares and I was like 'this is just incredible'. It's something you can't miss out on if you come here.

"They're very big on basketball and football. I know a lot of people play basketball, and I see kids playing in the parks around with hoops. Basketball may even be bigger than football here because I've also seen a couple of clips from Red Star-Partizan basketball games and that looks crazier than the football. Somehow, in an indoor arena, they're setting off flares! I don't know how it's allowed but it looks really good."

More players are being encouraged to step out of their comfort zone

"As much as it may sound quite daunting - and it's definitely a big step, especially if it's your first move away, it's one that takes a lot of consideration - but your career realistically is so short compared to other professions. I think it's a blessing that you're able to have these opportunities. People may dream of one day saving up to move to these countries, and you can do it by playing the sport that you grew up loving to play. I think it's such a blessing and one that you definitely shouldn't take for granted.

"It's definitely not one to overlook if a foreign club comes in for you, even if it's somewhere you're not looking to go. Maybe Serbia wasn't in my top three choices, but I think still taking that risk and taking that leap will allow you to experience something really special. I don't think you're going to look back. I definitely encourage anyone that's even having a one percent thought of doing it to just take it with both hands and go for it."

Scenic destinations in Austria, Germany or Switzerland hold plenty of appeal

"I've never really been fully fussed about playing Premier League football week in, week out. It would be nice to play in England again but it's definitely not something I'm rushing to do or saying after the season I have to go back to England.

"I would love to stay in Europe. For me personally, I would love to play in somewhere like the Swiss League or Austrian League or Bundesliga, Bundesliga 2, because I like hiking, I like mountainous regions so I would love to live in a country like that where I can go training and then take a bus or take a train to the mountains and just have a walk. It would be so special and I think if I ended up somewhere like that, I would be completely happy to stay there for the rest of my career because that's the life I want to live.

"At the end of the day, football is football, it's my job, not who I am. There's other stuff that I want to do and other stuff that I value more than my job. So if I was able to get an opportunity like that, I would happily take that move and I would happily stay there."

How life in Serbia ranks across five important areas

Weather: 7/10. "I haven't properly experienced the winter yet. It's cold now, but I've heard it gets absolutely freezing. That's the first thing they said when I got here, they were saying in some regions it drops to minus 20 Celsius! Obviously coming in the summer, it was a nice warm summer, and now autumn moving into winter has been mild, doesn't really rain too much. We're having a bit of a rainy spell now, but it's great for football. Maybe people visiting might find it a bit annoying but overall I'd say the weather's really nice."

Food: 8.5/10. "They have really nice food here. That was one thing I didn't really research before I came. I was a bit worried and a bit skeptical, but I eat most things anyway and I'm happy to try new things. Some of the food is really nice - they have a lot of local pastries, the coffee is really nice. They do a lot of barbecue meals. We went out as a whole team for a barbecue and it was so good. It's something you wouldn't really get in the UK, you have to experience it here or in the Balkans region. I haven't had a single complaint with the food yet."

People: 10/10. "They're really friendly, really welcoming. My team-mates welcomed me straight away. Even going to the shop, and I'm squinting trying to read certain things, getting up Google Translate, people will happily walk past you and help, ask what you're looking for. They speak really good English. If a foreign person came to the UK, sometimes you know the conversation is a bit tricky, but they really try their best when speaking to a foreigner here. Obviously I can't speak much, I can't really have full conversations, so they really do try when it comes to English and that's really thoughtful. I couldn't complain a single thing about the people, they're all lovely and amazing."

Things to do: 5/10. "It depends on what you're looking for. I've heard that the nightlife is really good. I don't go out personally so I wouldn't know. A lot of the nature is really nice. But if you're looking for activities, I personally haven't seen many that have piqued my interest. It depends on the person. Some people enjoy things that some other people don't. Like when my girlfriend was here, for example, we didn't really find many activities that we both wanted to do but going shopping is really easy, going for a walk, going to the fortress. There's a zoo in the centre, there's loads of escape rooms. That's not really my cup of tea but I know for people visiting they would really enjoy the city."

Cost of living: 8/10. "Taxis are nice and cheap, there's a free bus service. If you're traveling through Belgrade, if you want to go into the centre, I'm pretty sure you can get a free bus. Food and drink are all really cheap. Certain shops are a bit cheaper here than in the UK - some brand shops are a bit cheaper here which is good. You just have to make sure you've got your converter up because a couple times I've looked at the price and been like 'oh, that looks like it would be cheap' and then I convert after I paid for it and I've paid so much more than I thought! That's one thing I would say, just make sure you have a rough idea of how much you'll spend and maybe set aside a bit of a budget so you don't overspend with the different currency over here."

#2704. 3 things that led to the Mavericks’ cathartic 116-94 blowout win over the Golden State Warriors

The Dallas Mavericks (8-7) handled business Wednesday night, beating the shorthanded Golden State Warriors (8-7) 116-94 in a game Dallas controlled almost from the start. Cooper Flagg led the way with 33 points, five rebounds, nine assists and three steals on 11-of-15 shooting, while P.J. Washington added 21 points and hit five threes. Kyrie Irving finished with 17 points, six rebounds, five assists and three steals, and Dallas shot 50.6 percent from the field and 41.5 percent from distance. Golden State never found much offense without Stephen Curry, Jimmy Butler and Kristaps Porzingis, and once Dallas pushed the lead to 20 by the end of the third quarter, the game was essentially over.

Dallas jumped all over Golden State in the first quarter, starting with Flagg and Irving controlling almost everything. The duo scored or assisted on 22 of the Mavericks' first 25 points, setting the tone for a 19-2 Dallas run that quickly created separation. Flagg was perfect in the quarter, scoring 10 points on 3-of-3 shooting, while Kyrie added six points and two assists. P.J. Washington also caught fire early, hitting all three of his 3-point attempts, and Dallas shot 57.1 percent from the field and 50 percent from deep. Golden State, meanwhile, looked lost offensively for long stretches and shot just 38.5 percent. The Warriors found a little life late, but Dallas still led 35-25 after one.

Golden State showed more resistance in the second quarter, but Dallas remained firmly in control. The Warriors forced a few sloppy turnovers and cut into the lead, but Flagg quickly settled things down. He scored 12 points in the quarter and reached 22 by halftime, attacking the rim, getting to the line, and knocking down another three while shooting 7-of-9 overall. Washington was just as important, finishing with 16 points, four threes, and another reliable source of offense for Dallas. The Mavericks shot 53.8 percent from the field, 45.5 percent from three, and went 10-for-10 at the line in the half, taking a 62-49 lead into the break.

Dallas blew the game open in the third quarter and turned a comfortable lead into a rout. The Warriors were shooting just 41.4 percent from the field and 25 percent from three through three quarters, with Brandin Podziemski struggling badly from deep. Dallas kept stacking stops, moving the ball and getting quality looks, and by the end of the quarter the Mavericks had pushed the lead to 20 at 92-72. At that point, the game was over.

The fourth quarter was basically a formality. Dallas had already put the game away in the third, so the final 12 minutes were mostly about getting through it healthy and letting the bench finish things off. Flagg stayed in just long enough to finish with 33 points, five rebounds and nine assists, and the Mavericks cruised to a 116-94 win. Golden State never seriously threatened again, and Dallas emptied the bench to close out a pretty uneventful final quarter.

Flagg had been in a rough stretch by his standards over the last few games, so this was about as emphatic of a response as Dallas could have asked for. Flagg was in control from the opening minutes and finished with 33 points, five rebounds, nine assists and three steals while shooting 11-of-15 from the field, 3-of-5 from three and 8-of-8 at the line. He was aggressive without forcing anything, got downhill whenever he wanted, and looked much more comfortable creating for everyone around him.

The nine assists were especially encouraging because they showed he wasn't just hunting his own shot to break out of the slump. He read the floor, made the right play, and controlled the game. After a few quieter performances, this looked much more like the version of Flagg Dallas has come to expect.

Washington needed this one too. His jumper had gone cold during the road trip, but he looked completely different against Golden State, knocking down five threes and finishing with 21 points on 7-of-10 shooting. He hit three threes in the first quarter alone and helped Dallas create separation before the Warriors could settle into the game. When Washington is making shots like this, the Mavericks become so much harder to defend because teams cannot load everything toward Flagg and Kyrie Irving. It was only one game, but seeing the ball go through the net again should be a nice confidence boost after the way he had been shooting.

There really is not much more complicated than this — Golden State doesn't have much if the Warriors don't have Curry in the lineup. The Warriors were without Curry, Butler and Porzingis, but Curry's absence was especially obvious because Golden State had almost no reliable way to generate offense. The Warriors shot 42.7 percent from the field and an ugly 23.7 percent from three, with Brandin Podziemski going 0-of-5 from deep and Yang Hansen Lendeborg finishing 6-of-18 from the field.

Dallas deserves credit for taking advantage, but there were long stretches where Golden State simply looked incapable of creating a good shot. Once the Mavericks pushed the lead out in the third quarter, nobody on the other side could drag the Warriors back into it. This was a shorthanded team that looked exactly like one.

#2703. D.J. Reed returns to Lions practice

#2702. NFL Week 11 Injury Report: Drake Maye likely done for season, surgery for Jordan Addison

Staying up to date on NFL injury news is of the utmost importance for fantasy football success. The article below tracks all fantasy-relevant players currently listed on their team's injury report and provides fantasy managers with actionable recommendations as new information rolls in.

Check back for updates from Tuesday through Saturday.

**UPDATED AS OF WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 18 AT 8:15 PM ET**

Impact: Likely none, though the Bills will employ a run-heavy approach against the Dolphins.

Palmer managed only seven offensive snaps in Week 8 before departing with an aggravation of the hamstring injury he has battled since Week 4. He was placed on injured reserve.

Impact: Not much, honestly. Palmer has played sparingly this season in a situational role, although his absence could leave room for Skyler Bell to be active for the third time this season. The Bills also activated Tyrell Shavers (knee) from the reserve/physically unable to perform list. He could join the wide receiver rotation but does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

Achane suffered a torn ACL in the team's Week 3 loss to the Chiefs, ending his season.

Impact: Achane's unfortunate season-ending injury creates opportunity for Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright. The timing of the injury makes it likely that Achane is able to fully recover before the start of the 2027 regular season.

Impact: Kyle McCord's installation as the team's starter hurts all involved. Until we see how McCord fares in this system, only Ollie Gordon is a safe FLEX starter.

Bell is listed as doubtful for Week 10 against the Colts. He is day-to-day entering Week 11. Impact: Bell has largely been unable to get anything going during his rookie season, with the team leaning more heavily on Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas (shoulder), who was limited to begin Week 11. Bell's status could afford Kevin Coleman Jr. additional opportunities, although the low-volume Miami pass offense remains unlikely to support more than one pass catcher, now playing with a backup quarterback in Kyle McCord.

Maye is believed to have suffered a fractured ankle, an injury that would sideline him for the remainder of the 2026 season. Impact: As of Tuesday, the team continues to gather more information on the injury sustained in the first half of the Week 10 loss to the Lions. The team is also reportedly reaching out to quarterbacks as they look to right a sinking ship following consecutive losses for the first time in head coach Mike Vrabel's tenure. More to come on this developing story. Suffice to say, the fantasy value of the primary skill position players in New England takes a significant hit for the remainder of the year.

Doubs was placed on injured reserve following a shoulder injury sustained in Week 6. He will miss the next four games, at minimum.

Impact: The Patriots have now played only 33 offensive snaps with both Doubs and A.J. Brown on the field together this season after Doubs was injured on his second offensive snap in Week 6. Brown returned from injured reserve in Week 6 and should have the runway to return WR1 numbers while Doubs remains sidelined.

Brown missed Week 8 and Week 9 with ankle and knee issues before returning for Week 10 against the Lions, only to pick up a hamstring injury. The team is reportedly gathering more information during their Week 11 bye.

Impact: DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, Mack Hollins, and Kyle Williams led the team in snaps and routes in the absence of Brown in Week 9, with none of the bunch consistent fantasy producers. Fantasy managers are likely forced to wait until more information is released to gauge Brown's expected status in Week 12.

Henderson was placed on injured reserve ahead of Week 10 and will miss the next four games, at minimum.

Impact: Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner are likely to form a one-two punch in the absence of Henderson, with Stevenson the favorite to lead the team in opportunities and snaps. Stevenson can be viewed as a volume-backed RB2 for the time being.

Smith departed the team's Week 10 loss with an ankle injury. Follow-up testing confirmed the injury is not considered serious but his status for Week 11 against the Chiefs is in doubt. He was officially limited on Wednesday.

Impact: The fantasy upside of all primary skill position players for the Jets would take a significant hit should Smith be unavailable against the Chiefs. Fantasy managers will want to monitor this situation closely in the coming days.

Cooper aggravated the same ankle injury he has been dealing with for multiple weeks in Week 10, placing his status in doubt for Week 11. He was sidelined to begin the week.

Jackson returned from an ankle injury in Week 8 and made it all of one offensive snap before suffering a thumb injury that is likely to sideline him for the remainder of the regular season.

Huntley suffered a season-ending turf toe injury in the team's Week 8 loss to the Bills.

Smythe suffered a torn Achilles in the team's Week 4 win over the Titans. His season is done.

Higgins saw his 2026 season taken from him due to a torn ACL suffered in camp.

Pierce aggravated the injury that required offseason surgery in Week 2. The Colts placed him on injured reserve in Week 3. He will attempt to avoid surgery by rehabbing his injured heel. Head coach Shane Steichen said he is unsure whether Pierce will play again this season.

Kenneth Walker’s groin injury will keep him out for at least another day.

Head coach Andy Reid told reporters in his press conference that the running back is one of a few players who won’t practice on Wednesday.

“He’s got a sore groin, so it’s getting better. But with those … you don’t want to do something stupid, going out there,” Reid said. “It’s still bugging him a little bit. But he’s feeling a lot better than he was.

“We’ll just see. It’s a day-to-day thing, so we’ll see how it goes.”

Walker did not practice last Friday before missing Sunday’s victory over the Falcons. Rookie Emmett Johnson rushed for 101 yards and had six catches for 70 yards with two touchdowns in Walker’s stead.

Additionally, Reid said right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) and right guard Trey Smith (concussion protocol) will not practice on Wednesday.

The full first injury report of the week for Kansas City will be released later in the day.

#2700. Nets rocked by lowly Bulls in ugly night to forget

That's how the Nets described the 137-107 butt-kicking they took from the Bulls on Wednesday night in front of a sellout crowd of 17,548 at Barclays Center, humiliated on the home floor.

Not by Chicago. But by their own lack of fight. Of fortitude.

Patrick Williams shoots over Danny Wolf during the first half of the Nets' 137-107 blowout loss to the Bulls on Nov. 18, 2026, at Barclays Center. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST

"That was embarrassing. Been in the league for 13 years, and that's one of the worst games I've ever been a part of. And not because of the score … but it's how we did it. That wasn't cool. Nothing about it was cool," Julius Randle said. "We've got to find a way to figure out the root of it or whatever, but that's just unacceptable."

"It's just a pride, an effort, the competitive spirit, all of that, it was nonexistent."

The Nets (3-11) scored the first bucket and never led again, trailed by 37 at home, got shredded defensively and once again got punched in the face and never hit back.

They never even got up off the mat, allowing 53.5 percent shooting and 21-for-45 from deep.

"Very disappointed, and it was just starting with effort. We were not a competitive group, we were not a connected group, we were not a selfless group," Nets coach Jordi Fernández said. "So, I saw selfishness, I saw pointing fingers, and I saw guys that didn't always play hard."

The most galling part was after Monday's loss to the 76ers, they talked about having to punch first. Randle reiterated that at Wednesday morning's shootaround.

Brooklyn head coach Jordi Fernández reacts during the first half of the Nets' blowout loss to the Bulls. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST

But the Nets haven't been able to walk how they talk.

Asked if his message wasn't getting through, Fernández said, "I can try to say it in Spanish because the English didn't understand. So I'll keep trying and find whatever language works, but yes, the effort was not good."

In the past few days, the Nets have suffered one-sided beatings at the hands of both the Grizzlies and now the Bulls, routs that reflect poorly on their own rebuild and raise real questions about the big picture.

But Randle said this is less about players having to look to Fernández for messaging and more about having to look in the mirror.

Julius Randle drives past Jalen Smith (25) and rises up for a dunk during the Nets' blowout loss to the Bulls. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST

"Nah, as a man, you've gotta look yourself in the mirror, come in to work and figure out what matters. When winning is what matters, then we'll do the necessary things for that," Randle said before admitting, "but no, it's not there right now."

Egor Dëmin had 22 points, four assists and four rebounds, while Nolan Traore added 13 points and four assists. Mikel Brown Jr. scored a dozen of his 15 in the fourth quarter, with the game well out of hand.

But leading scorer Michael Porter Jr. was worse than invisible, too conspicuously poor to hide. He had just five points on 1-for-7 shooting and left the locker room before the media got inside.

The Nets gave up 25 to Matas Buzelis, and Josh Giddey (18 points, 14 rebounds, nine assists) just missed a triple-double. Ex-Net Nic Claxton added 14 off the bench.

It was another failure against a team they're measured against.

Memphis tanked last season to land Cam Boozer, whom the Nets had liked. The Grizzlies are now 11-4 after wins over Golden State, Portland and now Cleveland.

But at least getting blown out in Memphis was understandable. These Bulls are terrible, and played without rookie Caleb Wilson (hand injury).

The Nets came into Wednesday with an identical mark to Chicago and another chance to measure themselves against another rebuilding rival. And once again, they were found wanting.

"It's just unacceptable by us, by everybody, not just one individual, everybody," Brown said. "Stuff like that just can't happen, it's just unacceptable. #2697. NFL slams NBC's Mike Florio, Chris Simms for 'offensive' Mike Vrabel joke

The NFL is not happy with one of its primary media partners.

During a recent episode of "Pro Football Talk Live" on NBC Sports, Mike Florio and Chris Simms made a joke at the expense of New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel that included a thinly veiled reference to Adolf Hitler, although neither mentioned his name.

"He got the German mustache to go along with that right now, too," Simms said during a Nov. 17 edition of the show while discussing the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions on Sunday in Munich, Germany. "So he was hitting all themes there over in Germany."

"You gotta be careful trimming that thing," Florio said. "Yeah, if you're in Germany, you gotta be careful trimming the sides of that thing."

Between a lot of laughs, Simms and Florio kept the bit going for a few more seconds, although an off-air producer must have appeared to wish the duo didn't go down that road.

"It was eighty years ago," Florio said. "Let us have some fun, for crying out loud."

The exchange did not sit well within NFL headquarters.

"We found the remarks inappropriate and offensive," the NFL said in a statement to USA TODAY Sports from executive vice president of communications, policy and public affairs Jeff Miller

Both Florio and Simms contribute to NBC's elbow coverage of "Sunday Night Football." Simms had previously been part of "Football Night in America" but was removed from the show this offseason. The duo apologized Thursday.

"On yesterday's (Nov. 17) PFT Live show, we made comments that some found offensive and we apologize," Simms and Florio said in a joint statement via NBC Sports.

Playing without Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and Dean Wade, the Sixers looked to be on their way in the early going to one of those losses you just chalk up to being shorthanded on the road, trailing Orlando, 40-27, after one quarter. The Sixers are now 13-3 on the year with the last-place Bucks coming for a visit to Philadelphia on Saturday. Let's talk Bell Ringer.

VJ Edgecombe: 24 points, 8 rebounds, 6 assists, 2 steals, 4 turnovers

While the "Edgecombe's development is being hurt" narrative is nonsense, I do understand the desire to play out an alternate timeline where VJ gets his usage ramped up in his sophomore season. We caught a glimpse of it Wednesday night with Maxey and Brown out and it sure was fun to watch. Edgecombe had the ball in his hands a lot more often and did a group job creating shots for both himself and his teammates. Manchester United have appointed Mauricio Pochettino as their new manager after years of links and speculation. The Argentine coach arrived at Carrington yesterday afternoon after flying directly from the United States on a private jet.

Naturally, his focus will be on preparing his side to take on Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, and he has brought his own coaching team along. Pochettino often works with the same group of people for years and shows his great faith in his team around him.

Here is an introduction to who United's new coaches are.

Jesus Perez and Miguel D'Agostino – Assistant coaches

Both Pérez and D'Agostino are trusted lieutenants of Pochettino.

They have been with him for every job since Espanyol. Therefore, like the head coach, they have experience of Premier League football through jobs at Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea.

They also worked together while at Paris Saint-Germain. Pérez was a fitness coach at Espanyol but has been an assistant manager since getting a promotion at Southampton in 2013.

He is from Barcelona and is 41 years old.

D'Agostino, on the other hand, is from Argentina and used to be a defender. He played for Newell's Old Boys amongst numerous South American sides in a playing career spanning from 1989–2003.

He has been an assistant coach since 2002 with Canet Roussillon, Brest and Dubai CSC before joining Pochettino at Espanyol in 2009.

Jiménez is 56 years old and also played, but in Spain. He came through FC Barcelona's academy but played over 200 times for their local rivals Espanyol.

Jiménez also spent three years at Atlético Madrid. The former goalkeeper also represented Spain three times and won Olympic gold in the 1992 Barcelona Olympics in football.

Like Perez and D'Agostino, he has worked with Pochettino since his Espanyol days and at every club since.

Pochettino's son was born in Barcelona and is just 31 years old. In 2017 he was appointed fitness coach and sports scientist at Tottenham Hotspur, making him the youngest sports scientist in Premier League history.

He has worked with his father at Spurs, PSG, Chelsea and USA. The coach can speak English, Spanish and French, which will make him popular in the United dressing room.

Silvia Tuya – Strength and conditioning coach

Tuya joined up with Pochettino while working for the United States national team. Tuya holds a doctorate of science in high performance and is fluent in English, Spanish, and Catalan.

Tuya will make history as Manchester United's first female coach for the men's side. She has previously lectured at the University of Barcelona and National Institute of Physical Education of Catalonia before joining Pochettino's USA set-up in October 2024.

She also worked briefly at FC Badalona in her native Catalonia, the team competing in Liga F – the top flight of the women's game in Spain. Fans will hope both Tuya and Pochettino's son can cure the issues the club has suffered from with injuries and a general lack of fitness in comparison to Premier League rivals.

As an analyst, he will be responsible for shaping training and opposition reports. Scott was working with the United States national team, but United have poached him.

#2687. Cavs react to Sam Merrill’s tough missed free throws: ‘We all trust him’

CLEVELAND — There's no tougher way to lose a basketball game than at the free-throw line. It's even worse when the culprit is arguably the best shooter on your team.

For Sam Merrill and the Cleveland Cavaliers, tonight was one of those losses.

Merrill came up empty on a pair of free throws with the Cavs trailing by one point to the Memphis Grizzlies and under 5 seconds to play. That isn't what you expect from a career 89% free-throw shooter.

Even so, the Cavs aren't upset with their sharpshooter.

"I mean, there's a reason I made the pass [to Merrill]," said Donovan Mitchell. "We all trust him, you know, and I would do it again tomorrow; I'd do it again the next night; you're not defined by two free throws at the end of the game."

Sometimes you make the right play and things don't work out. Mitchell was doubled by Memphis in the final seconds; that's why Merrill had the ball and was crashing towards the rim with a trailing defender. It was the correct approach from everyone — the final shots just didn't go in.

"I love the process; I love that he drove, he's so smart to drive the ball, that's what I look at," said Kenny Atkinson. "This is the sport, right? It happens to the best, but I loved how he got to the line."

None of that makes the loss feel any better. But, for what it's worth, the Cavs feel comfortable with the opportunity they had in front of them. It seems like they'll win that scenario more often than not.

It's also true that Cleveland had other avenues towards winning tonight's game. They couldn't get key stops in the fourth quarter, and Merrill wasn't the only player who missed a shot.

"I told him we're not in that situation if I knock down the corner three or if I hit the floater that I missed," said Mitchell. "So we can all point to something."

The beauty of basketball is another opportunity is almost always right around the corner. The Cavs have a fast turnaround with another home game against the Indiana Pacers on Friday.

"For [Merrill], go get 30 in a half against Indiana, and we'll be fine," Mitchell joked.

#2686. USMNT's Record World Cup Run Pulled In 30M+ US Viewers

The USMNT's 2026 World Cup didn't just rewrite the program's record book. It rewrote the US television ratings book, too. Pochettino's side went 2-0-1 in the group stage, won a World Cup knockout match for the first time since 2002, and then lost to Belgium in the Round of 16 in front of the largest American audience ever assembled for a non-NFL broadcast.

What happened is now well documented on the field. The USMNT kicked off its FIFA World Cup 2026 campaign with a resounding 4-1 victory against Paraguay, then beat Australia 2-0 to secure Group D. The team finished with a program-best six points and a record eight goals in a single World Cup, then beat Bosnia and Herzegovina 2-0 in the Round of 32 for its first knockout win in 24 years.

The numbers behind the screen were just as striking. The Bosnia win pulled in more than 24.4 million viewers on Fox, peaking near 32 million, the most-watched soccer telecast in English-language US history at the time. That record didn't last. The Round of 16 exit to Belgium averaged a preliminary 30 million viewers on Fox, peaking at over 41 million — the most-watched non-NFL telecast on any network since the 2016 World Series Game 7 on FOX.

Part of this is simple math: home-soil kickoff times with no time-zone penalty, and a tournament format that gave the US three winnable group games before a signature knockout night. But the on-field product did the heavier lifting. Pochettino rotated aggressively — the lineup from the second game to the third featured nine changes, the most ever for the USMNT between two World Cup matches — while still finding goals from six different scorers across the tournament, keeping casual viewers tuned in even when the team shuffled personnel.

That depth mattered against Bosnia specifically. The US played over half an hour a man down after a Balogun red card, yet still closed it out — the kind of game that turns neutral channel-surfers into committed viewers for the next round.

A single tournament doesn't permanently reorder the American sports hierarchy. The NFL remains the dominant force by any measure, and World Cup ratings traditionally fade between cycles. But the scale here is new: the group stage alone averaged nearly 5.1 million viewers across 72 matches on Fox, FS1 and Tubi, a 92% increase from 2022, making it the most-watched English-language Men's World Cup group stage in US history.

For MLS, the implication is less about instant crossover and more about exposure. Millions of casual viewers who tuned in for Balogun, Pulisic and Reyna now have a reference point for American soccer talent heading into a league already expanding its footprint. Whether that attention converts into sustained MLS or USMNT viewership outside World Cup years is the real test — and it's the one that will determine if this tournament was a ceiling or a new floor.

While one Lions player is out, another is on his way back in.

Detroit announced on Wednesday afternoon that the club has placed defensive end Aidan Hutchinson on injured reserve and activated safety Kerby Joseph off of the reserve/physically unable to perform list.

Hutchinson suffered a torn ACL during the Lions’ victory over the Patriots in Munich on Sunday. It’s the second season-ending injury in the last three years for Hutchinson, who missed most of 2024 with a fractured tibia and fibula.

Joseph has been sidelined by knee issues that limited him to six games last season. He was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice. Head coach Dan Campbell has said that Joseph is expected to play against Tampa Bay on Sunday.

Additionally, the Lions have re-signed defensive back Nick Whiteside to the club’s practice squad.

#2683. Fantasy Football Rankings: Hayden Winks' RB Blueprint for Week 11

The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically everything that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can. There will be this RB column, a WR column and a combination column on the onesie positions. You will find film notes and endless charts. Maybe enough charts to stress test the Yahoo website. I kid.

It's impossible to get every ranking thoroughly early in the week, so be sure to keep checking in on these columns through Sunday morning. As always, my full rankings at every position are available.

1. Jahmyr Gibbs (vs. TB) - 127.5 proj. total yards

Gibbs is the 1.01 in fantasy points over replacement per game (+15.9) and only trails Jaxon Smith-Njigba in winning percentage on Yahoo. Seems good.

Tampa Bay has been stout against the position, ranking 32nd in half PPR points allowed to opposing backfields and holding recent primary rushers like Bijan Robinson (RB28), D'Andre Swift (RB50), Chuba Hubbard (RB34) and Jaylen Warren (RB23) in check. Detroit heads into the home matchup with an implied total of 25.25 points (ninth) as 7-point home favorites. It's a difficult spot, but it's getting nearly impossible to not have him as the RB1 overall every week.

The Chiefs seem to be planning for Kenneth Walker III (groin) to rest another week after Johnson more than held his own in last week's blowout win. The rookie, who reminds me of a Bucky Irving type on film, handled 22 carries and six receptions, leading to 32.1 half PPR points on 20.6 expected points. Those are obviously elite RB1 numbers. Kansas City simply doesn't have another RB it trusts for the moment, and the offense is firing on all cylinders against mediocre opponents.

The Cardinals are just that. They've allowed the fifth-most rush YPG (130) and were just schooled by Blake Corum (119 total yards) last week. A huge 28.0-point team total as 15.5-point favorites (!!!!!!) awaits.

3. James Cook III (vs. MIA) - 110.5 proj. total yards

Cook ranks as the RB6 in half PPR points per game on RB8 usage across his last four contests, averaging 23 carries (second) and 109.8 rushing yards per game. He has scored a rushing touchdown in each of his last four games (what's new?), including a season-high 157 rushing yards on 18 carries in Week 10.

The Bills are expected to beat the Dolphins by 16.5 points with a bonkers 31-point team total. Miami just lost DTs Jordan Phillips and Zeek Biggers to injured reserve. I don't have to tell you this is a great spot.

4. Christian McCaffrey (vs. MIN) - 87.5 proj. total yards

When McCaffrey is in the United States of America this year, he averages 22.7 half PPR points (RB2) on 16.3 expected half PPR points (RB6). Turns out, Kaelon Black is a fine role player but nothing more than that to CMC. Remember to go outside in early September while the weather is nice.

Anyways, this will be a great test for the 49ers as they face the Vikings in Mexico City. They've been run on at times and won't have LB Blake Cashman, but that's about as negative as I can get on what otherwise is an elite defense. They've been fifth best against fantasy RBs this year (16.7 half PPR per game), though fantasy RB1s have held the line; James Cook III (RB7), Jahmyr Gibbs (RB5) and Jonathan Taylor (RB8). We can ding CMC's projection with the Niners projected for 24.25 points versus their current 31.75 points per game, but it can only go so far. He's a mid-range RB1.

5. Chuba Hubbard (vs. BAL) - 109.5 proj. total yards

The Ravens defense has been one of the more underwhelming units. Their secondary has been better than their run defense, to the point that even Omarion Hampton ran well up the gut against them last Monday night. It's a shorter week for Baltimore, who is now trending out of the playoff picture. We'll see how much fight it has left. The Panthers have a 23.0-point team total (12th) as near-field-goal favorites.

6. Javonte Williams (vs. TEN) - 94.5 proj. total yards

Let's keep this simple: Williams is an upside RB1 whenever the Cowboys have a 31.5-point team total, as they do here.

The Titans have allowed nearly 1,500 yards over their last three games, the most in a 3-game stretch in their franchise history. Trading away mega-star DT Jeffery Simmons and Pro Bowl-caliber S Amani Hooker won't help. The starting RB against Tennessee has cleared 100 total yards in four straight contests.

7. Bucky Irving (at DET) - 85.5 proj. total yards

This assumes Jalon Daniels is back at QB with Baker Mayfield (foot) picking up a new injury during the bye week. The Bucs are likely going to be extremely run-heavy, as they've been for the past two months with the OL smoking defenses up front. Irving has been the RB7 on RB11 usage this season, with 21.0+ half PPR points in 4 of 5 recent games. He's averaged 22.2 carries during that stretch, with games against pretty easy opponents. That's too big to fail, especially given how slippery he is on tape.

The Lions are a pass funnel typically, but the losses of LB Jack Campbell, EDGE Aidan Hutchinson and CB D.J. Reed (questionable) make them fairly bad in both phases. They still have some DTs to worry about, but the Bucs should be able to run it here, despite the spreadsheets suggesting otherwise. Tampa Bay will attempt to bleed out the clock as 7-point road dogs with a team total of 18.25 points (21st). Irving should absorb a lot of that team total.

8. Derrick Henry (at CAR) - 78.5 proj. total yards

The Ravens are going to pass more with Jacoby Brissett at QB and with the OL struggling, especially when first-round rookie LG Vega Ioane isn't on the field. Henry can still score goal-line touchdowns as he did on Monday night, but a real reset is warranted in terms of efficiency and rushing volume if the Ravens aren't expected to be crushing teams as often as they would've with Lamar Jackson, who is hoping to return around Week 16 if things go to plan. In the meantime, it's possible Henry catches an extra target or two based on the scheme changing, but that won't even out the loss of projected touchdowns. He'll settle in as a boom-bust RB2 the rest of the way.

The Panthers have cleaned things up with better health and a new DC recently, but Carolina has bled fantasy points to RBs (24.8, third) across the season. It was Jonah Coleman (RB6) two weeks ago and Josh Jacobs (RB11) and Bucky Irving (RB2) before that. A 21.0-point team total isn't the worst thing this week, with six teams on bye and five others projected for fewer than 17.0.

9. Jonah Coleman (vs. LV) - 99.5 proj. total yards

With R.J. Harvey (knee) on IR, the backfield has been down to just two. Coleman leapfrogged J.K. Dobbins over the last pair of games, finishing as the RB7 and RB9 in expected half PPR points. Dobbins won't play on passing downs, so Coleman is grabbing some receptions alongside his rushing role. He has been just fine on tape in a good situation.

Speaking of, the Raiders are generous when it comes to fantasy points for RBs. They've allowed, oh, just 176 rushing yards per game this month. Both Seahawks RBs played well behind three backup linemen, and CMC (RB4), Braelon Allen (RB7) and Kyren Williams (RB12) were fantasy RBs this month. Denver is listed as 10-point home favorites with an implied team total of 25.25 points (eighth).

10. Tony Pollard (at DAL) - 85.5 proj. total yards

Pollard has been the RB8, RB3 and RB1 most recently, and it's simply been because he's breaking a ton of tackles. It's hard to believe it'll be sustainable, as star LG Peter Skoronski is on injured reserve, but Pollard is also the RB10 in expected points this month, with Cam Ward taking his game up a tier. It's still a painful offense on the whole and the floor can fall out at any point. It's best to stay tethered to his RB15 on RB16 usage standing across the entire year sample. Hopefully Carnell Tate (shoulder) can return to make the offense more potent.

The Cowboys are pathetic on defense. They've removed their sitting DC from play-calling duties, while their starters have missed a ton of tackles in crucial spots. They also don't play sound against the run, which is why they've allowed the most fantasy points to RBs (27.0) and most rushing yards per game (154) this season. Last week's 44.3 eruption from Christian McCaffrey against them was the best fantasy outing of the year by any player at any position. Beyond that, opponents facing Dallas have passed at a 47% rate in neutral situations, which is the third-lowest neutral pass rate allowed in the league. Tennessee enters as 8.5-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 23 points (13th).

11. Chase Brown (at WAS) - 74.5 proj. total yards

The Bengals have largely abandoned the run, which arguably isn't even a bad thing for Brown. Cincy is up to 30.9 points per game because it's first in passing success rate. Brown has a better chance of lucking into touchdowns if the team passes its way down to the goal line. We saw that happen last week when each of his scores came through the air, both out of structure.

Aside from the scores, Brown tallied eight receptions as a check-down option with space to operate, as defenses are going to have to play softer and softer coverage against these alien WRs. Brown can be forgettable as a talent on a severely pass-heavy offense, and still finish as a low-end RB1 in fantasy due to the scoring bonanza. He's the RB1 in receptions per game (5.2).

The next victim of the Bengals' offense will be the Commanders, who don't have two of their top DTs and were struggling through the air before anyway. The Bengals are up to a 30.5-point team total.

12. D'Andre Swift (vs. NO) - 83.5 proj. total yards

Kyle Monangai (toe) is back. Here are Swift's splits with him since Week 5 of last year, when the offense became the version we have today.

For context, 13.9 half PPR points is the RB16 right now, while 13.0 expected points is the RB17. Those are probably closer to his per-game floor the rest of the way, but it is a real reset for Swift's baseline projection. He can still have RB1 moments with Monangai. They will just happen less often.

The Saints are a great spot to sneak in a fantasy RB1 moment! They've allowed the second-most fantasy points to RBs on the sixth-most rushing yards per game (130). Chuba Hubbard ran right through tackles last week, something that's happened way too often this year. Chicago has a monster 30.0-point team total, so both backs are obvious starts.

13. Jaylen Warren (at PHI) - 95.5 proj. total yards

Warren has settled in as an upside RB2 with Rico Dowdle back in the mix. He's averaged 14.0 carries and 2.8 receptions this month, leading to RB17 on RB19 usage. The Steelers haven't played great ball on offense over that stretch and just watched LG Mason McCormick dislocate his ankle last week. The OL being great this season has certainly helped Warren, who has been a top-5 RB to my eyes this year beyond that.

The matchup is reassuring. This is an eruption spot, looking at the EPA numbers on the ground. The Eagles have struggled all year, then traded away run-stuffing DT Jordan Davis at the deadline. There are fewer reasons to be afraid of what used to be an impossible opponent, and the lines reflect that. Pittsburgh enters as 4.5-point road favorites with an implied team total of 21.5 points (15th).

14. Bhayshul Tuten (at NYG) - 92.5 proj. total yards

Tuten set a career high with 28.1 expected half PPR points last week, with 26 carries and three receptions. Many of those were failed goal-line attempts, but Tuten did score late en route to an RB10 on RB1 usage outing. He's now the RB10 on RB17 usage this season as a low-end RB1 with weekly upside. Chris Rodriguez Jr. will vulture the occasional touchdown, but otherwise, it's all Tuten now. The only marginal issue is that the already suspect Jaguars OL is now missing C Robert Hainsey (knee) for the next couple of weeks.

The Giants rank 25th in half PPR points allowed to opposing RBs at 17.1 points per game. That includes ranking 23rd in points allowed on RB rushing plays (11.3 per game) and 20th on RB receiving plays (5.8 per game). Opposing lead rushers have routinely been held in check against them recently, with no RB clearly the top-24 over their past three games. DROY favorite Arvell Reese has a lot to do with that. Jacksonville heads on the road as 6-point favorites with an implied team total of 26.25 points (seventh). It's more of a mediocre matchup for Tuten.

15. David Montgomery (vs. IND) - 67.5 proj. total yards

Montgomery got in a full practice last Friday before being ruled out, but has practiced in full leading up to Thursday Night Football this week. Woody Marks (concussion) won't play, leaving Monty with Emari Demercado, who missed some lanes in the second half of last game. It won't be a surprise if the desperate Texans use Montgomery as a bell cow despite him being out since Week 5. They don't have a real choice. Of course, the Texans' bell cow RB hasn't been very valuable so far. Since Week 6, the Texans RBs are averaging 16.8 expected half PPR points per game with very mid efficiency. Montgomery finishing with 15-20 expected points shouldn't come as a surprise this week, considering the opponent.

The Colts haven't been competitive all year, especially without their best linemen on both sides of the ball. This month, Indy has allowed the sixth-most rushing yards per game (144). This season, they've allowed the sixth-most points to fantasy RBs (23.0). There really are no excuses for Houston this time around. They own a 28.5-point team total at home as 12.5-point favorites.

16. Omarion Hampton (vs. NYJ) - 71.5 proj. total yards

Hampton set season highs in fantasy points (17.0 half PPR) and usage (15.9 expected) last week, in their first win of the year. Hampton handled 22 carries in a run-heavy game plan that continued because the scoreboard finally allowed for it. The Chargers are first in neutral run rate (61%), so don't be surprised if Hampton's fantasy performances tick up if they can stay more competitive after a brutal schedule. You can see the extra carries in the second half of last week here:

On tape, Hampton was used slightly differently last week. He handled nine pitches, which is the second-most by a player in a single game all year. Instead of being pointed to the perimeter, many of them got him going straight downhill, where his attributes are maximized. They also ran more man concepts instead of the wide zone stuff OC Mike McDaniel typically calls for. It's a meeting in the middle between player and coach, one that was long overdue.

This week, the Chargers are favored. I repeat, the Chargers are favored against the Jets. They don't have their best run-stopping DT right now either, which has helped opposing teams rack up 154 rushing yards per game this month (fourth). James Cook III (RB7) and Kenneth Walker III (RB1) just went nuclear against them, but even Ollie Gordon II had 103 total yards and a score in Week 7, too. This is easily the best it's looked for Hampton since the games started this year.

17. Saquon Barkley (vs. PIT) - 75.5 proj. total yards

Barkley is impossible to get a grasp on due to his injuries, the moving parts on the OL and now Joe Milton at QB. In a part-time role on a lousy offense in three games before the bye, Barkley was the RB25, RB21 and RB20 on RB26 usage. He looked good when he was on the field, and the OL did seem to be in a bit of a better spot on tape. I can see him out-kicking those marks after the bye, which hopefully has allowed him to get healthier. The Eagles' offense is in a spot where they can fully clunker at any time, so the floor doesn't exist.

The matchup will be a challenge, of course. Milton versus the Steelers' pressure will put the team in bad spots. Pittsburgh is only allowing 83 rushing yards per game (30th), as teams have essentially stopped trying to run on them in neutral situations (61% pass, first). Philly can't afford to do that, so it'll be running into brick walls for Barkley, with the hopes he springs a few of them for explosives. A 17.0-point team total works against those odds. Barkley is a volume-based RB2 in the most optimistic of projections.

18. Cam Skattebo (vs. JAX) - 70.5 proj. total yards

Skattebo is back to bell-cow work with Tyrone Tracy Jr. on IR and Najee Harris released. Devin Singletary failed in that role when Skattebo missed in Week 9, then Skattebo delivered an RB5 on RB6 usage outing in Week 10 against the Commanders. They've had extended rest to get Skattebo prepared for another heavy workload in a balanced offense. It won't be surprising to see Skattebo emerge as a fantasy RB2 for the rest of the way, especially if his three grabs from Week 10 hold up.

The Jaguars defense has been stingy to opposing backfields, ranking 29th in half PPR points allowed to RBs. They did concede an RB8 weekly finish to Tony Pollard in Week 10 without DT Jordan Davis and safety Jessie Bates active, though Jonathan Taylor managed just 4.7 points (RB37) against them in Week 8 when they did have a star run-stuffing DT. Opposing offenses have leaned heavily into the pass against Jacksonville with a 59% neutral pass rate (second highest). I doubt the Giants will do that too much given their coaches and personnel, but it's a difficult matchup regardless. New York enters as 6-point home underdogs with an implied team total of 20.25 points (18th).

19. Breece Hall (at LAC) - 70.5 proj. total yards

Hall has been the RB16 and RB21 in usage since returning from a quad injury. He's easily paced Braelon Allen in touches and played more receiving snaps last week after being eased in the game prior. Hall will stick in the 14-18 touch range most outings, while splitting the goal line role with the more downhill Allen. That'll put a cap on Hall's projections each week, but as long as Geno Smith is healthy, the OL is in good enough shape for them to remain balanced on offense. Hall is a fine RB2, while Allen is a shakier FLEX, even during the byes.

The Chargers represent an above-average matchup overall (duh), ranking 11th in half PPR points allowed to opposing RBs at 21.1 per game. Los Angeles is sixth in points allowed on the ground, though they rank 27th against backs via the air. They're still without Derwin James. New York travels out west as 3.5-point road underdogs with an implied total of 19.0 points (19th).

20. Kyle Monangai (vs. NO) - 55.5 proj. total yards

In 18 games with D'Andre Swift since Week 5 of last year, when the Bears offense ascended to the spot they are today, Monangai has averaged 9.9 half PPR points on 10.0 expected points. That's closer to his lower-end outcome at this point, and the Bears seem antsy to get Monangai back so they can begin spelling Swift after a stretch of too much volume. In four games this year, he's the RB16 (14.2) on RB21 usage (12.6 expected).

Fresh off the bye, the Bears should be at the peak of their powers. A date with a Saints team that can't tackle awaits. Chicago projects for 30.0 points. Monangai is an upside FLEX, possibly a straight-up RB2 given the constraints of the week.

21. Ollie Gordon II (at BUF) - 74.5 proj. total yards

Gordon is now playing with fire after ripping off explosives as a new starter back in September. He's down to RB25 on RB13 usage this past month, thanks to 20 carries and just 1.5 receptions per game. His efficiency could crater without Malik Willis, as it did last week when he was the RB18 on RB10 usage. Trickier defenses than the Colts will give Kyle McCord more trouble.

The Bills are waking up on defense with a new DC. They've seen multiple true breakouts from their DL, and they're more shored up at S with Amani Hooker in the mix and moving Cole Bishop more into the box where he's at his best. Even while going through some pains, the Bills are still only allowing 93.6 rushing yards per game (25th). It's a bad matchup for Ollie with a team total of just 14.5 points.

22. Jonathan Taylor (at HOU) - 76.5 proj. total yards

Taylor is no longer a fantasy RB1. Over the past month, with Seth McGowan earning more change-of-pace work, Taylor has dropped to RB16 in usage at 12.9 expected half PPR points per game. This matches the historical splits I mentioned last week based on how many points the Colts finish with. When Indy is held to under 21 points, Taylor is largely a fantasy RB2. Last week, McGowan converted a goal-line score on a drive Taylor was playing on. Taylor was stuffed on another drive's goal-line attempt, but it's no longer true bell-cow usage for Taylor.

Beyond that, the Colts ruled out both of their starting OTs and obviously traded away star LG Quenton Nelson the weeks prior. Having all of this backup talent on a short week against the Texans' DL is beyond concerning. The Colts have a 16.0-point team total as 12.5-point dogs. With a real receiving corps and a healthy OL in Week 3, Taylor was held to 68 scoreless yards against Houston. He also had 39 scoreless yards against them in Week 18 with a backup QB.

#2678. GTA 6 comes out before Raptors can break losing streak vs. Wizards

It's been nearly 13 days since the Toronto Raptors last won a game.

The slump continues after the Raptors fell to the Washington Wizards 103-99 on Wednesday.

On a night when the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto 6 is released to the public, here are four takeaways from the game, partly to lighten the mood in Toronto, and also to make you wonder how long fans will have to wait before the Raptors get back into the win column.

One of the main attractions of GTA 6 is the ability to switch between the two new protagonists Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos. Both players move through the campaign as a unit, but they also have their own unique set of skills, story beats, and responsibilities.

The same goes for Immanuel Quickley and Jamal Shead, especially as the point guards on a night without Kawhi Leonard, Scottie Barnes and RJ Barrett.

As the lone guard on the court, both Quickley and Shead were exceptional. Quickley finished with a team-high 25 points on 42.8 per cent shooting. He also added five assists and four made threes.

"We're just playing together. We're short a lot of guys, we can't just do it with one person," said Quickley. "We did a pretty good job of moving their defence around and gave ourselves a chance to tie it in the end."

Meanwhile, Shead led both benches in scoring with 15 points.

As in prior games this season, the duo was also deployed as a backcourt tandem. After losing the opening 12 minutes 29-23, Quickley and Shead were instrumental in helping Toronto win the second and third quarters.

Outside of the main heroes, there is a litany of new side characters in GTA 6 destined to take their seats alongside some of the franchise's most iconic figures. Brian Heder (landlord and smuggler) serves a narrative clutch, allowing Jason and Lucia to live rent-free during the game.

At Scotiabank Arena, rent comes in the form of wins and success, and it's unfortunately past due.

While Allen Graves hasn't been able to properly capitalize on his 13-point performance against the Boston Celtics on Nov. 11, the rookie is slowly coming along after 15 games and is on track to be the Raptors' most important "brand-new" side character.

"They're instilling a lot of confidence in me throughout this whole process," said Graves. "I feel like as each game goes on, I'm just getting better and better and understanding it more."

Graves finished with nine points and five rebounds while playing a career-high 31 minutes. He also shot 50 per cent from the field.

"You have to study film but being in the game is the best experience you can get," said Graves. "The more I'm in the game, the more I can go out there and make mistakes and learn from them."

In the second quarter, while Toronto was in one of its signature droughts, it was Graves who provided the spark. From the left wing, Graves' dribble-drive resulted in two points. Moments later on defence, his relentless motor powered him to poke a ball loose for an offensive rebound. On the ensuing offensive possession, Graves' strong finish at the rim resulted in two more points.

His tenacity and hustle alone convinced Raptors head coach Darko Rajakovic to play him 14:18 in the first half, marking a new career high through two quarters for Graves.

"He matched up in similar situations with Trae Young and he was matched up with Anthony Davis," said Rajakovic. "For him, those minutes are super valuable."

With Collin Murray-Boyles exiting the game at halftime due to illness, Graves started the third quarter. He immediately rewarded Rajakovic's trust in him by scoring the first bucket of the half with a leaning jumper from the left block.

GTA has always been about the side missions as much as it has been about the main storyline.

Without several of the Raptors' main weapons, the team needed its auxiliary options to step up. Jamison Battle and Ja'Kobe Walter answered the call. Truthfully, they didn't have a choice after being inserted into the starting lineup.

Battle has comfortably transformed into the clear-cut best shooter on the roster, but he's now also showing a flair for the dramatics. His three-pointer at the buzzer just before the half was theatrical. But when he used a Trayce Jackson-Davis screen on the left wing before knocking down an off-the-dribble three-pointer, it definitely opened some eyes in the building. Battle finished with 19 points.

"It's controlling what we can control," explained Rajakovic. "Our preparation, our work, our intentionality, how hard we play and compete."

Walter also added 18 points of his own, including three triples. His perimeter game is a known commodity, but it was his contributions across the board that were impressive. Walter tied his career-high in assists (6) and also added seven rebounds, trailing only Jakob Poeltl (9) on the team.

Unfortunately, Walter's glaring miscue occurred in the closing minutes, when on the fast break, he dribbled the ball off his foot and out of bounds.

Battle had a chance to tie in the end but was unable to sink the three from the top of the arc.

There's a plethora of new game mechanics that fans of the GTA franchise have spent the last year gushing over. It's fitting that several Raptors went deeper into their bag of tricks on a night that GTA 6 finally releases.

It started with Quickley, who did less probing and more attacking on the offensive side of the ball. He frequently resorted to step-back jump shots, pull-up dribble jumpers, and turnaround fadeaways.

On defence, Quickley even drew a charge to stop a Wizards 2-on-1 fast break late in the third quarter.
