#2673. Recap: Wizards mercifully win 103-99 vs. Raptors

The Washington Wizards finally got back on the win column on Wednesday in a 103-99 contest versus the Toronto Raptors at Scotiabank Arena.

The Wizards ended their losing streak before it reached nine. However, it was hard to feel good about the performance, given how shorthanded the Raptors were coming in. Toronto played without Kawhi Leonard, Scottie Barnes, and RJ Barrett, and also lost Collin Murray-Boyles before halftime due to illness.

The Wizards started things the way most fans would have wanted. A pair of AJ Dybantsa dunks helped Washington race to a 12-6 lead early. Anthony Davis feasted in the interior, scoring 10 early points and grabbing 7 rebounds. The good guys led 29-23 after one.

Washington kept showing a lack of discipline on defense. The team repeatedly made the right rotations for 15 to 20 seconds before allowing timely cuts or extra passes to burn them. Our guys were putting in the work but clocking out before the shift was over.

The Wizards also gave up 9 offensive rebounds and committed 10 turnovers through two quarters. The last giveaway came via a sloppy pass from Trae Young to Davis that led to a Raptors three-pointer to beat the halftime buzzer. The team was fortunate to be up 49-47 entering the break.

Young was invisible for most of the game. He didn't score his first field goal until he connected on a 32-foot three-pointer at the 1:11 mark of the third quarter to give Washington a 76-73 lead.

The Wizards also failed to take advantage of the Raptors committing their fourth team foul with over 8 minutes left in the third. Washington only earned bonus free throws in the final minute. The Wizards trailed 79-78 entering the fourth.

If there's one positive in this game, it was seeing how much fight Dybantsa displayed to get the victory. He scored 9 emphatic points in the final period, flashing the top-shelf athleticism that made him worthy of the No. 1 overall selection.

The Wizards built up a 10-point lead with 2:49 to play, finally pulling away from a Raptors team far inferior to them on paper. A sloppy finish to this one gave Toronto a chance to tie the game in the final seconds, but Washington survived for the 4-point win.

I'd advise any Wizards fan considering watching the game on delay to steer clear of the final three minutes for your own sanity. Stick to Dybantsa highlights on YouTube.

AJ finished with a career-high 23 points and notched his first NBA double-double with 12 rebounds. Davis led all scorers with 25 points, while Kyshawn George poured in his usual 20 points and 4 threes.

The Wizards head to Chicago next for a rematch with the Bulls on Friday night.

#2670. Max Verstappen on F1's WHOOP plan: "It's nobody's business, I don't even know my heart rate"

Ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix, Formula 1 announced a partnership with WHOOP. A number of drivers will wear the company's health trackers, with their data being shown live during TV broadcasts in 2027.

The latter, however, remains entirely optional, leaving the decision up to the drivers themselves. According to those behind the initiative, at least a handful of F1 drivers have already committed to the project, but Max Verstappen is clearly not among them.

During the media day in Las Vegas, the four-time world champion made it clear that, in his view, his personal data is nobody else's business.

"I won't be involved. I don't use any device, also not for my training, I don't use anything. First of all, I don't like to be tracked and I know when I'm tired," Verstappen said.

"If other drivers want to [share], then sure. But for me, it's not something that I like and also not something that I want people to see or that I want to show."

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing

Not all drivers are opposed to the idea, however. Charles Leclerc, for example, has already indicated in Vegas that fans can expect to see his data during live broadcasts next year.

"I don't have anything to hide in particular. Obviously, I'm now an ambassador for WHOOP and I've been using the device for quite a long time now to track my recovery, my sleep, but also when I'm in the car," he said.

In a sense, Leclerc is even pleased with the deal, as it is now formally permitted to wear the device while driving. Ferrari already had a partnership with Whoop, but drivers no longer need to wear the trackers discreetly while driving.

"Now there's an actual device that is certified by FIA that we can, without hiding it anymore, wear while driving. It's a good thing, at least for me, it's very useful. To show it to everybody is another matter that we'll for sure discuss, but I personally don't have any problems with it."

Mercedes driver George Russell sits somewhere in the middle and mainly believes that the data needs to be viewed in the right context. He is not as firmly opposed to the idea as Verstappen, but sees both perspectives: as a fan, he would appreciate it, but as an athlete, he has his reservations.

"As a neutral, if I was sat on the sofa, I think I'd really enjoy seeing it. But everyone's different. A 45-year-old's heart rate is probably going to be quite a bit lower than an 18-year-old's heart rate," he said.

"And when you're sat on the grid, you'll be saying, Fernando Alonso's ice cool when the lights are going out because his heart rate is much, much lower. But if you put my dad in the car, who's 72, his heart rate's going to be even lower than Fernando's. And even people of the same age have different heart rates as well."

According to Russell, there is therefore a risk that fans will see the figures and draw the wrong conclusions from them.

"I didn't really know how it could be additive, if that makes it, because we're all just so different," he said. "But it's going to create a narrative that's going to be positive for some [and negative for others]. I'm lucky that I'd say my heart rate's on the lower side, but I would empathise with a driver whose natural heart rate sits 20 beats higher than somebody else.

"So yeah, from a neutral, I think it's cool, but as the athlete, I'm not going to say no. I think it's okay as we are."

Kimi Antonelli: Yo-yo racing to return at F1 Las Vegas GP

Max Verstappen: "If they let me write the rules, F1 wouldn't be allowed in certain places"

#2666. Rapid Recap: Heat 137, Bucks 130

In the first matchup since the biggest trade of the summer, the Miami Heat took it to the Milwaukee Bucks all night, and despite the final score being decided by single digits, the Heat led by over 20 for the majority of the game. Giannis led the Heat with 27 points, 13 rebounds and nine assists, while Ryan Conwell led their bench scorers with 13 points. Meanwhile, Tyler Herro struggled mightily in his return to Miami, scoring just eight points in a dud of a game while Kyle Kuzma led Bucks starters with 26 points. Brayden Burries had an impressive night, scoring 20 points and grabbing seven boards, while Kasparas Jakucionis led Milwaukee off the bench with 20 and five helpers.

The energy and perhaps nerves were palpable at the start of the game. Immediately after Klay Thompson's first three-pointer, Brayden Burries drove through the paint, drew a foul, and put Milwaukee on the board. Neither team got many paint touches through the first half of the quarter, and the game came down to made three-pointers. Miami continued its assault from deep, while the Bucks showed some solid ball movement; after a 35-second possession that produced three offensive rebounds, Jakucionis finally put it away with a layup. Miami made 18 of its first 23 field goals from three, and the Bucks got shots from all over the floor, though much less effectively. The first quarter ended with Miami up 34-23.

Burries carried the load early in the second with five quick points and a steal to keep the Bucks within shouting distance, but the rest of the team offered little help, and before you could say, "GTA 6", the Bucks were down 20. As Heat coach Spoelstra began to stagger his bigs, it felt like the game got more out of control for Milwaukee. Bam Adebayo terrorized the Bucks, scoring from pretty much anywhere, and just when you thought the visitors might get a break with Bam checking out, Giannis checked back in. By the four-minute mark, though, Giannis was just 0/1 from the field with 2 points and five assists. That said, GA took what the defense gave him and found the open man in the corner more often than not. The Heat made just four shots in the paint in the quarter but kept raining fire from downtown, shooting 6/10 from beyond the arc. The Bucks entered halftime down big, 74-48.

If there was one positive from the first half into the third, it was that the Bucks didn't look totally lost in the paint. Coming into the game, the expectation was that Miami's frontcourt would be too much to handle, but Milwaukee did pretty well there. Thankfully, through the first four minutes, the Heat were held to just two 3-pointers, which let Burries put up eight quick points after scoring back-to-back threes and giving the Bucks a sliver of hope. Burries continued to try to bring life to the starting lineup, but ultimately his efforts were not enough; other than Kuzma, the other three starters combined for just 12 total points through three quarters. Despite the Bucks scoring 38 to keep up their league-leading offensive pace in the third quarter, Miami matched it with 38 to stay up big, 112-86.

Miami had been shooting 34.3% from three for the season, but tonight they couldn't miss, going 22/48 while the Bucks shot just 14/41. Despite the huge lead, Miami didn't start subbing their starters out until later in the quarter, and to their credit, the Bucks kept the energy high and the pressure on. Milwaukee went on a 12-0 run led by Jakucionis and Caris LeVert, who saw his first minutes of the season and looked great, scoring eight points in the quarter. Of course, Giannis checked back in and pulled his team's lead back out to 20 in short order. However, credit to Jakucionis, Ament, and Green for keeping the energy up; the Bucks outscored the Heat 18-5 to close it out, but it was too little, too late.

43: the total number of shots the Bucks made, which, despite being down by 20-30 for most of the night, was 3 more than the Heat. This game was decided from downtown, and the hail of three-pointers from Vice City Miami completely overwhelmed the Bucks.

The Bucks need to trade Tyler Herro urgently. Herro may be the only trade chip the Bucks have outside of Jaime Jaquez Jr., and the sooner Milwaukee makes this trade, the sooner they can more permanently give crucial developmental minutes to the other young Bucks, who set a better tone than the veterans seem capable of.

#2659. Cooper Flagg was as good as the Warriors starters were bad in blowout loss in Dallas

Or just looking at the starting lineup versus the reserves. The Warriors' starters fell behind 21-9 before Steve Kerr made his first substitutions of the game. After halftime, the Dallas Mavericks started the third quarter with a 16-4 run against those same starters. That's a 24-point deficit in about 10 minutes, and it essentially decided the outcome quite with 20 minutes left to play in a 116-94 Mavs win.

I was tempted to start typing gibberish for the first 10 percent of this recap just to best capture the feeling of watching the Warriors right now. And then the sub-headlines, phot captions, and tagging would be incredible, the recap equivalent of Will Richard coming off the bench to score 20 points and collect four steals to finish +8 in 27 minutes, meaning the Warriors were -30 with him on the bench. For the record, I do not have a fully-torn UCL in my thumb

Sophomore sensation Cooper Flagg scored 33 points on just 15 shots, going 11-for-15 making all eight free throws. He also had nine assists and five rebounds in one of the most impressive performances we've ever seen from a guy who wears a t-shirt under his jersey. PJ Washington scored 21 points, made five threes, and blocked three shots. He and Flagg were both +32.

Kyrie Irving tormented the Warriors but what else is new? He had three steals, like Flagg, scored 21 points, and had five dimes, playing 29 minutes.

After the Warriors dug themselves into a 25-9 hole, the reserves got them back into the game by closing the quarter on an 11-4 run, highlighted by two threes from Gary Payton II. The bench simply played with dramatically more energy than their counterpoints in the starting lineup, as evidenced by the backups grabbing 10 of the team's 14 steals — De'Anthony Melton had three of them.

Richard and Gui Santos were displaying so much hustling that Jennifer Lopez is in talks to play Santos in the film version. During the second quarter, Richard and Draymond Green combined on a steal, but Santos got stripped on the subsequent fast break. Seconds later, Richard knocked the ball away again, and Santos dove on the floor to get the loose ball, flinging it forward for a Richards layup. Richard also took in a steal for a slam all by himself.

How long did it take Warriors announcer Bob Fitzgerald to begin complaining about the Mavericks' three-point shooting success, based on a small sample size? Just over eight minutes of game action, when Dallas was 4-for-8 from deep. Oddly, Fitz brought this up after two Mavs misses had dropped them to 4-for-8 from deep.

Fitzgerald returned to this topic four minutes into the second quarter after Cooper Flagg made a three to beat the shot clock while being closely guarded by Will Richard. "I mean, if that's going in, you gotta be kidding me!" Fitz declared. After the Warriors forced a turnover, not by Flagg, Fitzgerald continued, "Will Cooper Flagg miss a shot tonight?…That three had NO chance of going in, and went in!" (Flagg was 5-for-5 at the time)

#2657. The real reason John Harbaugh opted to receive after Giants won coin toss

John Harbaugh was prepared for a curveball just minutes before kickoff.

The Giants — like most NFL teams — typically defer their choice to the second half if they win the opening coin toss. But they broke from the norm last game by choosing to receive.

Because of some strategic advantage specific to the Commanders?

No, because cornerback Tae Banks wouldn't have been ready if the Giants started the game on defense, backup Colton Hood was already banged up (dislocated finger) and backup Paulson Adebo was a healthy scratch.

It shows the level of thought and quick-thinking adjustments needed to be an NFL head coach.

"We had a little issue come up right before, in warmups, where … actually Tae got dinged on his shoulder, and he was getting looked at," Harbaugh said.

"So we weren't going to have him for the first series. So that being the case, we figured hopefully he'll be out here for the second series."

Gregory Desrosiers returned the opening kickoff 24 yards, and the offense picked up two first downs before punting.

"Offense was gracious enough to at least put some plays out there and buy some time," Harbaugh said, "and [Banks] was able to play. So that determined that decision."

Giants head coach John Harbaugh speaks at a press conference in East Rutherford, N.J., on Nov. 18, 2026. Robert Sabo for NY Post

#2652. Stats Rundown: 4 numbers to know from the Mavericks 116-94 win over the Warriors

The Dallas Mavericks (8-7), fresh off a three-game losing streak, needed some home cooking on Wednesday night and got it in a big way. Dallas got a convincing 116-94 win over the Golden State Warriors on a night where the Mavericks celebrated the life of former head coach Don Nelson. This was a big win for a team that looked to be finding its way during a three-game winning streak, only to immediately appear listless in a follow-up three-game losing streak. The Mavericks looked locked in, hit the gas and never really let up in an effort that gets them over .500.

Cooper Flagg cracked the 30-point mark on a free throw early in the fourth quarter. That gave Flagg his 15th career 30-point outing, good for second place in league history for 30-point games recorded by a teenager. Flagg now trails LeBron James by five such games and has 33 days remaining as a teenager to match or exceed James' total.

If there is an object lesson as to how the 3-point shot influences the modern NBA game, this was it. The Mavericks drained 17 shots from deep to the Warriors' nine. The point differential almost exactly matched the point differential on the scoreboard. Beyond the comparison of made shots are the small adjacent details. The Warriors missed 29 longballs, connecting on just shy of 24% overall. It's difficult to overcome such a deficit on the makes, but giving up that many possessions to misses leads to points the other way.

Speaking of 3-point shots, Washington was in peak form, draining 5-of-7 on the night. His 71.4% shooting from deep is unrealistic in the long term, but if he could keep his off nights around 33% and pepper in some of these scorching hot nights, the Mavs will have a whole new dimension to their offense. If he can cement his consistency in this department, it's going to give the opponent fits.

The game was a clean sort of sloppy. Yes, that's an oxymoron of epic proportions, but speaks to the overall flow of the game. The turnovers were of the type where players just constantly jumped the passing lane and took off the other way. It lent itself to an overall flow of the game back-and-forth, but it was a lot! The Mavs had 19 turnovers and the Warriors nearly matched them with 17 of their own. 19 is simply far too high, and the Mavs are fortunate the Warriors couldn't capitalize on the miscues. In the end, the Warriors had 21 points off turnovers where Dallas had 18.

#2651. Eagles claim Cowboys draft pick off waivers

The Philadelphia Eagles claimed Ajani Cornelius off waivers from the Dallas Cowboys, according to an official team announcement.

Cornelius, 24, is a 6-5, 318 pound offensive lineman who was selected with a sixth-round pick (No. 204 overall) in the 2025 NFL Draft.

Playing college football for Rhode Island and Oregon, Cornelius almost exclusively played at right tackle. Pre-draft scouting report via NFL.com:

A durable lineman with NFL traits and four years of starting experience, Cornelius lacks standout flashes on tape. He has been a full-time right tackle but lacks protection talent to stay outside as a pro. He has access to physical tools but needs to play with better bend and hand quickness to help stabilize his play. He can cover up defenders with size but is frequently out-leveraged at the point of attack. His average body control and slide quickness should be mitigated in smaller spaces but those issues will still be concerning against explosive interior rushers. The traits should make him a Day 3 target, but his ceiling might be as a backup.

During his time with Dallas, Cornelius logged zero offensive snaps and 21 special teams snaps over four regular season games played. He played at right tackle during the 2025 preseason before the Cowboys moved him to right guard in the 2026 preseason.

The Eagles seem to think Cornelius has some developmental potential. It also makes sense for them to add some more offensive tackle depth after waiving Fred Johnson.

As an added bonus, the Eagles might've snagged a player the Cowboys were hoping to get back on their practice squad.

#2645. Heat transform arena for ‘GTA 6’ theme night — complete with massive rooftop advertisement

MIAMI — Jennifer Alvarez was at work inside the building where the Miami Heat play when she scrolled her way into a video almost by accident.

The trailer for "Grand Theft Auto VI" — loosely based in Miami — found its way onto her screen. It included an image of what clearly was the arena where she happened to be at that moment, plus a few more city landmarks.

An idea was born. Alvarez got on her phone.

A Vice City theme announcement is projected at the Kaseya Center before the Heat's 137-130 win over the Bucks on Nov. 18, 2026 in Miami. AP Photo/Marta Lavandier

More than two years, countless meetings and thousands of hours of planning later, the Heat — having pulled off a collaboration with Rockstar Games, which developed and published "GTA VI" — were at the epicenter of the launch of arguably the most anticipated video game of all time. On Wednesday, the Heat became Vice City, playing against the Milwaukee Bucks on a one-time-only court wearing one-time-only uniforms.

"We waited in the rain for two hours," said Paola Boivin, carrying her newly acquired Vice City jersey with Heat center Bam Adebayo's No. 13 on the back shortly after the arena doors opened Wednesday. "So worth it. So worth it."

Alvarez, the senior vice president for brand and chief growth officer for the Heat, said the team worked tirelessly to turn the building into a real part of Vice City. For one night, she said, fans weren't from Miami or Florida. They were from Vice City and Leonida.

"What we're doing is creating a crossover experience of gaming and sport in a way that no one has actually interacted with before," Alvarez said.

Vice City is the fictional center of the game, loosely based on Miami. Leonida is the state, loosely based on Florida. And the Heat have been known for their "Vice" line of uniforms and apparel since debuting the brightly colored, widely popular gear in the 2017-18 season.

It was a perfect match. Vice meets Vice City.

A neon Vice City sign glows at Kaseya Center during the Heat's win over the Bucks in Miami on Nov. 18, 2026. REUTERS

"We thought: 'Wait a minute. This is us. How do we figure out a way to be a part of this?'" Alvarez said. "It's the return of Vice City, which is a highly anticipated title — 13 years people waited for this game. And we've been synonymous with the word Vice since 2017 when we first introduced the original Vice campaign and knew we needed to work. We needed to reach out. There's just too much here, too many kind of stars aligning, too much kismet happening for us to ignore it."

Every detail for Wednesday — the day before the official global launch of "GTA VI" — was thought out.

The Vice City-themed court is displayed before the Heat's win over the Bucks in Miami. REUTERS

Miami-Dade County struck a $975,000 deal months ago to have "Vice City" atop the arena, a billboard of sorts for the countless passengers who will see it as they fly into and out of Miami International Airport. The game notes that the Heat provide to reporters before every game say Vice City. Doors to the arena opened earlier than usual, and once inside, some fans waited in line at various stores and kiosks for more than 30 minutes to buy Vice City jerseys. The jerseys were on sale for $120; by tipoff, some were listed on resale sites for more than $2,000.

The graphics inside the arena had "GTA"-themed twists and logos on the jerseys matched what gamers would see in "GTA." Public address announcer Gale Nelson broke from the usual script, referring to the team as "Vice City."

"We're all just running on pure adrenaline," Alvarez said.

An overall view of Kaseya Center before the Heat's win over the Bucks in Miami. NBAE via Getty Images

Heat coach Erik Spoelstra said he learned long ago that staying under the radar isn't possible in Miami — so when something like Vice City comes along, he embraces the circus.

"I think it's awesome. I think it's fun. It's 10x everything, and to have that opportunity in a regular-season game, I think is exciting," Spoelstra said. "I've never played the game before, but obviously I'm fully aware of it. And if they want to send me a console, I'll play. I'm curious now. I want to play."

There are elements of "GTA" within other video games. Later this month, the "NBA2K27″ game will debut a special Vice City Edition with Adebayo on the cover.

Fans walk past Vice City-themed decorations inside Kaseya Center during the Heat's win over the Bucks in Miami. REUTERS

"The culture of Miami is special and getting to see everyone experience that through the game is what's so exciting," Adebayo said.

Heat players, as a gift from Rockstar, got custom "GTA VI" consoles, controllers and the actual game on Tuesday, a thank-you for their part in the launch.

An overall view of Kaseya Center before the Heat's win over the Bucks in Miami. NBAE via Getty Images

The jerseys that the team were wearing Wednesday were delivered to the arena earlier this week, and the design of the court was kept quiet until Tuesday.

Milwaukee guard Tyler Herro, who spent the first seven years of his career in Miami and worked out Wednesday morning on the special court, already has the game downloaded.

People buy Vice City-themed Heat merchandise at the Kaseya Center on Nov. 18, 2026, ahead of the Grand Theft Auto VI release. AP Photo/Marta Lavandier

"I know what the Vice City means," Herro said. "I know the meaning behind it and obviously, 'GTA' is one of the most popular games. My kids obviously won't be playing it — keep them away from that — but it's a big opportunity for the city to welcome 'GTA VI.' Obviously, I'll be playing the game. I got to see what that's about."

The Heat launched a Vice City merchandise collection on Oct. 2; 30% of those orders have come from outside the U.S. ("We're shipping to 60 countries," Alvarez said.) Even the fast-food places that are seen in the video game — Burger Shot and Cluckin' Bell — have come to life at Heat games in recent weeks. The Heat offer arena tours to people when the team isn't playing; Alvarez said fans who come to those, without fail, ask if Burger Shot is open.

"And we're like, 'We're sorry, it's only open for games and events,'" Alvarez said. "This is global appeal. My hope is they come to a Heat game because we're a way for them to experience Vice City in a way they haven't been able to. So, it's my job to make their game experience unforgettable."

"I think in the past when I was younger, it would eat at me a lot more, just strictly the stat aspects," Bosa said Wednesday, via Nick Wagoner of ESPN. #2637. Nets embarrass themselves in front of franchise greats with pounding by Bulls

The Nets went back to their championship past Wednesday with ABA Night to honor their winning teams. Then they showed how far from a title they are.

The Nets took a 137-107 loss to the Bulls and embarrassed themselves in front of the greatest player to ever wear their uniform, with Julius Erving one of 10 living members of their 1974 and '76 championship squads being honored at halftime.

"We didn't really talk to the players, the coaches doing all the talking and they were getting their preparation in, doing all their drills … I fully anticipated the Nets to be so fired up having us here, they would blow Chicago out. I'm looking at 62-39, so I was wrong," Erving said during the YES broadcast.

"Two years in Virginia and three years in New York, I'd say those five years accumulated became probably the best years in terms of really enjoying the sport and learning and going through the process of developing," said Erving, who was raised in Hempstead and then Roosevelt.

"My days with the Nets, I'll never forget those. I'll always remember. It's where I started. This franchise has endured for 60 seasons, so I'm always going to have love for it. … One thing about basketball, it's truly a team game. When you see a 5-on-5 basketball game played well, it's poetry in motion. And the teams that were successful are the ones who recognized how to do it the right way."

But the Nets played the wrong way Wednesday.

The halftime ceremony included 10 of the 13 living members of the title squads: Erving, Brian Taylor, Bill Melchionni, George Bucci, Jim Eakins, Rich Jones, Jim O'Brien, Billy Schaeffer, Al Skinner and Chuck Terry. Kevin Loughery — the winningest coach in Nets history — was under the weather.

The beating the Nets took likely made their fans sick.

Julius Erving (left) and Al Skinner high-five at halftime during the Nets' 137-107 blowout loss to the Bulls on Nov. 18, 2026, at Barclays Center. NBAE via Getty Images

The Nets faced Nic Claxton for the first time after sending their longtime center to Chicago in a three-team deal that brought Randle back from Minnesota.

Claxton, who played 380 games — 297 starts — over his first seven years in Brooklyn, was looking forward to his return.

"Yes. I mean, that's just natural. You always want to look forward to playing against your former team. So, obviously add a little more juice to the game. Trades are part of the business. No ill will with this franchise," Claxton said.

Julius Erving speaks during a halftime celebration at Barclays Center on Nov. 18, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST

"There's no ill will at all, it's all good vibes. I don't have [anything] negative to say about anybody in this organization in Brooklyn. I'm grateful for my time here. I had a beautiful time here, cultivated a lot of great relationships. So it's all love."

Claxton finished with 14 points off the bench against his old team.

#2635. UConn coach Dan Hurley gets bucket-list game, but No. 12 Arizona earns 85-79 win

TUCSON, Ariz. (AP) — Dan Hurley called UConn's trip to McKale Center a bucket-list game.

It nearly turned into a Husky house of horrors.

Overwhelmed early by Arizona and the atmosphere, the third-ranked Huskies sputtered through an ugly first half that had the showdown between two of last season's Final Four teams looking like a beatdown.

Down 18 at halftime, the Huskies got back to playing UConn basketball in the second, pulling within eight before No. 12 Arizona pulled out an 85-79 victory in a game that felt like late March.

"Obviously, really disappointed, particularly the first half, just getting hit in the mouth like that. It rarely happens to us," Hurley said. "We're usually the hammer, not the nail."

Arizona's student section was full 90 minutes before tipoff, cascading boos upon Hurley the moment he stepped onto the floor and giving him a dose of what makes McKale Center one of college basketball's toughest road venues.

It's not the first time a Hurley has heard the vitriol inside this arena.

Dan's brother, Bobby, was rival Arizona State's coach from 2015-26 and drew the fans' ire every time he stepped on the floor or became apoplectic at a call he didn't like.

Bobby was the better player of the brothers, winning two national championships at Duke before playing five NBA seasons.

Dan is the more accomplished coach. He won consecutive NCAA crowns and led the Huskies to last season's title game.

Tommy Lloyd is building his own foundation at Arizona.

The longtime assistant to Gonzaga's Mark Few led the Wildcats to at least the Sweet 16 in four of his first five seasons in Tucson, punctuated by last season's first-in-25-years run to the Final Four.

"Obviously, they're out ahead of us with what they've accomplished," Lloyd said. "That's a program we're looking to see if we can kind of get in their shadow a little bit, maybe, follow their lead."

The early showdown between power programs was a rematch in a home-and-home series that started in Storrs, Connecticut, last season. Arizona won that game 71-67, though the Huskies were without big man Tarris Reed Jr.

Both teams were short-handed for the rematch.

Arizona had hoped to have forward RJ Godfrey in the lineup for the first time this season after a Pima County judge ruled him eligible for a fifth season. Instead, the drawn-out process strung out even more when the NCAA said it wouldn't comply with the judge's order.

UConn was without guard Solo Ball (wrist) and forward Nik Khamenia (foot).

There was still plenty of star power for UConn's first trip to McKale Center since 2017 with Kevin Ollie as coach.

Ivan Kharchenkov and Motiejus Krivas, key cogs in Arizona's Final Four run, were the tone setters.

Kharchenkov showed off his all-around game, bullying his way into the paint and hounding UConn players with physical-without-fouling defense.

Krivas, all 7-foot-2 of him, caused UConn problems at both ends, scoring at the rim, blocking shots, pinballing Huskies in the lane.

"The guy's nasty. He's mean," Hurley said of Krivas. "I told the guys he's like Godzilla. He ruins everything for you."

Derek Dixon, a North Carolina transfer, added to UConn's woes by going 3 of 5 from behind the 3-point arc. The combination gave Arizona a 47-29 halftime lead and the students added insult to Hurley's injury, serenading him with an R-rated chant.

Once the second half began, the Huskies were able to silence them — some.

UConn got back to playing physical defense, a Hurley hallmark, and held Arizona without a field goal for 6 1/2 minutes.

Braylon Mullins, a Huskies hero for his game-winning shot against Duke that sent UConn to the Final Four, handled the offensive end. Running defenders ragged off screens, he pulled up for 3-pointers and repeatedly got into the lane, scoring 19 of his 29 points in the second half.

Arizona ended up pulling it out, but UConn made it much harder than expected after getting dominated in the first half.

"It was crazy, it was hectic, it was chaotic," said Arizona freshman Caleb Holt, who had 19 points. "It was everything you dream as a kid playing a top-three team in the country."

The brutal-but-beautiful game gave Hurley a checkmark on his bucket list. He just wishes it would have ended better.

#2634. Nick Bosa: I don't think I've played my best football

49ers defensive end Nick Bosa’s only stats in Sunday’s 46-40 win over the Cowboys were one quarterback hit, four pressures and three penalties in 34 snaps. It was his fourth consecutive game without a sack, a first in his career.

But I don’t think I’m playing my best football right now, so that’s what gets to me more so than the actual stats.”

Bosa exited the injury report in Week 10. But he has worked his way back from the torn ACL in his right knee in Week 3 of the 2025 season and a calf injury in Week 3.

He has played catch up with new coordinator Raheem Morris’ scheme.

“I think there’s a learning curve and . . . a lot of guys haven’t had many reps in the scheme so far,” Bosa said. “I’m trying to break it down to the basics and just kind of get back. I missed a year and then missed camp. I kind of took for granted some of the things that I did automatically, and I thought I could just kind of coast and continue to do those things automatically and focus on other things. But I need to, especially with a newer defense, really hone in on the things that made me the player that I am.”

“I’m not going to make excuses because nobody really cares,” Bosa said. “But I’m going to get better and I’m pretty confident in that physically and how I’m playing.”
